Thanksgiving just got more expensive for the first time in four years.

The classic dinner for 10 now averages $58.63 — up 6% from last year, about $5.86 a plate (American Farm Bureau Federation, Nov. 2026). The 16-pound turkey does most of the damage: $23.68, up $2.38 — a 10% jump — on tight supply and strong demand.

North of the border it's worse: a turkey dinner for four is projected to cost about 10% more this year (Dalhousie University).

My take: $5.86 a plate is still a cheap way to feed a room — but a 10% jump on the one item everyone buys is the kind of sticker shock people actually feel.

What's your Thanksgiving table costing this year?
